image_description: A museum exhibit featuring the fossilized skeleton of a Triceratops. The image focuses on the skull, displaying the characteristic three horns (two large brow horns, one smaller nasal horn) and the massive solid bony frill. The ribcage and partial forelimbs are visible behind the skull. The bones are brownish-tan, set against a dark background with some museum infrastructure visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal structure clearly shows two large post-orbital horns and a smaller nasal horn, consistent with Triceratops anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows a fossil skeleton. The 'keratinous cutting edge' refers to soft tissue (beak sheath) which does not preserve in fossils. Only the underlying rostral bone is visible, so the checkpoint as described (keratinous edge) is not testable/present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible limb bones (humerus/radius/ulna area) are thick and columnar, consistent with weight-bearing quadrupedal limbs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The parietal-squamosal frill is massive and clearly extends well beyond the width of the facial portion of the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated like Chasmosaurus) and shows the rough texture typical of fossilized bone surfaces, with marginal undulations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeleton; no skin impressions or soft tissue are visible in this specific view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although the full hindlimbs are obscured, the visible forelimb structure is robust but shorter relative to the overall body height implied by the pelvis/ribcage position, consistent with the sloping posture.
The tail is completely outside the frame or obscured by the angle of the photo.
